newsitem.title: USA: NY/NJ Port Authority says to sell $100 mln bonds.
newsitem.headline: NY/NJ Port Authority says to sell $100 mln bonds.

text.p: Officials of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey said Thursday they plan to sell $100 million bonds in early July in a deal to be senior managed by Lehman Brothers.

"This is the one sale that we try to do once a year to bring in some of the smaller regional firms into a major Port Authority bond sale," Port Authority Treasurer Bruce Bohlen said following the authority's presentation at the Bond Buyer's Investor Forum. "So there are some 30-plus co-managers as part of this deal."

Lehman will serve as bookrunner, with PaineWebber Inc and Goldman Sachs & Co also serving as senior managers, he said. The deal is set for the week of July 7, with proceeds earmarked for capital improvements. The consolidated bonds, which will be subject to the alternative minimum tax, will be limited to a 20-year maturity, Bohlen said.
Bohlen said the limit is consistent with the authority's policy of limiting its AMT bonds to 20 years.

"This is a voluntary policy, it's not something we have to do, our typical bonds are 35 years," he said. The Port Authority sets a 20-year limit, "just because certain investors would probably agree that it would be prudent for us to do that in the sense that it's possible that after 2015 we might not have the airports."
While Bohlen expects the leases to be renewed, "it is a possibility that the airports could go back to the (New York) City in 2015."
"So given the fact that a lot of our AMT investment is in the airports, we're limiting the maturity," he said.

Already in 1997, the authority has done two $150 million consolidated bond offerings and a $934 million special project bond deal. The $934 million deal was for an international arrivals terminal at John F. Kennedy International Airport.

In addition to its July bond sale, the authority expects to sell $100 million to $150 million versatile structure obligation bonds, which is variable-rate debt, and another consolidated bond issue totaling $100 million to $150 million.
